bullets.title: MU: Blowout Q3 drives AI cycle reset; 16 SCAs worth $100B+ lock in multiyear demand
bullets.body: Micron reported F3Q revenue of $41.46B (+15% vs consensus $35.9B), non-GAAP EPS $25.11 vs $20.86, and gross margin 84.9% vs 81.7% consensus. Q4 guidance: $50B revenue and $31 EPS, both ~15-20% above consensus. Most importantly, Micron disclosed 16 Strategic Customer Agreements (~$100B minimum cumulative revenue, take-or-pay, 5-year terms, 20% DRAM and 33% NAND volume) with floor pricing 'well above prior cycle peaks.' Management stated supply-demand tightness extends beyond CY27 with no line of sight to catch-up. Price targets raised across the Street: Citi $1,400 (Buy), Wolfe $1,500 (OP), UBS $1,625 (Buy), KeyBanc $1,600 (OW), Mizuho $1,375 (OP), MS $1,200 (OW)—multiple analysts calling this a structural transformation of the business model.

bullets.title: SNDK: NAND cycle now tight through CY27; Citi raises PT to $2,500
bullets.body: Citi raises SNDK PT to $2,500 and initiates 90-day upside view, citing MU's guidance that NAND supply-demand tightness persists beyond CY27 and SNDK's own long-term NBM agreements locking in pricing. SNX (TD Synnex) F2Q26 revenue +31% YoY to $19.6B with strong Hyve AI server ramp; JPM raises PT to $325. WDC and STX also benefit from memory pricing momentum.

bullets.title: AAPL: Mac/iPad prices raised 15-25% on memory cost surge; demand destruction risk cited
bullets.body: Apple announced price hikes of 15-25% on MacBooks, iPads, and accessories citing 400%+ DRAM/NAND price increases from data center demand, with iPhone pricing unchanged but viewed as next. JPM noted the magnitude was 'more than our prior expectations'; AAPL fell 6% on the announcement as bears raised demand elasticity concerns. KGI downgraded AAPL to neutral. Multiple analysts note Apple's ASP historically 1.8-1.9x industry average provides some pricing power; bulls cite carrier installment plans as demand buffer.

bullets.title: GOOGL: AI talent departures to Anthropic/OpenAI; DJIA addition; antitrust/litigation risks
bullets.body: Google lost Nobel laureate John Jumper (AlphaFold co-creator) to Anthropic and Gemini co-lead Noam Shazeer to OpenAI during the week, driving GOOGL down 5% on June 22. GOOGL simultaneously joins the Dow Jones Industrial Average effective June 29, replacing VZ. MS streaming survey shows GOOGL YouTube as top-3 platform with strongest engagement. Antitrust expert calls suggest behavioral rather than structural remedies are likely from DOJ; PriceRunner damages case judgment postponed to July 1.

bullets.title: NVDA: Black market chip prices double; Rubin/CoWoS supply chain intact; Jalapeño unveiled with OpenAI
bullets.body: NVIDIA's DGX B300 chips more than doubled on China's black market amid export crackdowns. Separately, AVGO and OpenAI unveiled 'Jalapeño,' an LLM-optimized inference processor designed around OpenAI's vision; early testing shows substantially better performance-per-watt. MS raised NVDA CoWoS-L consumption estimate to ~910k units in 2027 (+40% YoY). Cerebras (CBRS) beat Q1 estimates and raised guidance; OpenAI ramp confirmed with Amazon partnership for 2027.

bullets.title: MSFT: Raises Xbox/365 prices on memory costs; Italian antitrust probe; technical breakdown
bullets.body: Microsoft raised Xbox console prices by $100-$150 (third hike in 13 months) citing 2.5x jump in memory/storage costs expected to double again by fall 2027. Italy's AGCM launched investigation over Microsoft 365 price increase disclosure practices. Technically, 22V Research rates MSFT Technical Score 0/4, below 200-day MA since February, with downside risk to $250 if $350 support breaks. EU Commission preliminarily designated Azure as a DMA gatekeeper alongside AWS.

bullets.title: CRDO: Evercore initiates Outperform at $325 PT as 'connectivity is the bottleneck' pure play
bullets.body: Evercore ISI initiated CRDO coverage at Outperform with a $325 PT, forecasting a 70% 3-year EPS CAGR with 2028 estimates 40% above Street consensus. CRDO dominates Active Electrical Cable (AEC) market and is applying a systems approach to optics with traction at TensorWave and Oracle. Customer base is diversifying, expected to positively impact P/E multiple. Stock rallied ~5-11% on the initiation.

bullets.title: ACN: Downgraded by multiple firms after managed services bookings collapse; buyback boost signal
bullets.body: Accenture posted -3% CC bookings growth in F3Q26 vs prior quarter's +1%, with managed services bookings down -15-16% YoY—well below investor expectations. TD Cowen cut to Hold, PT $150 from $258; Mizuho cut PT to $226. MS cut managed services bookings view and reduced PT to $130, citing potential AI crowding-out of IT spend. Counterpoint: ACN boosted FY26 buyback program by $2B to $7.5B (~10% of market cap), which UBS viewed as confidence signal; stock at 20-year valuation low at 8.5x 2Y forward P/E.

bullets.title: DKNG: Launches DKeX prediction market exchange; June PM volumes tracking $3.4B annualized
bullets.body: DraftKings launched DKeX, its proprietary prediction markets exchange, completing a vertically integrated PM offering. June consumer PM volumes tracking $200M+ monthly (up 80% from May's $110M) with $3.4B annualized consumer volume week of June 21, driven by World Cup. DraftKings has acquired 300-400k PM customers. JPM maintains Overweight; Citizens raised PT to $36. NY OSB GGR tracking -17% QTD on World Cup hold rate compression.

bullets.title: CCL: 2Q beat but FY26 yield guide cut 100bps on Middle East; 2027 bookings remain strong
bullets.body: Carnival Q2 adjusted EBITDA $1.58B beat guidance ($1.48B) and consensus ($1.48B) on significantly better cost performance. However, FY26 net yield guidance cut 100bps to +1.75% CC due to prolonged Middle East conflict impact on European sailings. Q3 yield guided +1.2% vs Street's +2.8%. 2026 now 93% booked at historically high prices; 2027 European bookings tracking mid-teens % ahead. UBS and Mizuho maintain Buy/Outperform; JPM OW at $43 PT.

bullets.title: NFLX: Down 6% on weak sub-add data and META Instagram TV competition; Wolfe initiates OP at $107
bullets.body: Netflix fell ~6% during the week as third-party data showed CCU growth decelerating and Meta expanding into long-form episodic content on Instagram TV. YouTube overtook Netflix in daily watch time (99 vs 93 min/day). Wolfe Research initiated Outperform at $107 PT (47% upside), arguing 19x 2027 P/E is attractive vs. 15% revenue CAGR. MS 16th streaming survey shows NFLX with strongest net retention score (+18) and 31% best original programming rating.

bullets.title: DLR/EQIX: Virginia data center tax immaterial; DLR announces $1.6B acquisitions
bullets.body: Virginia approved a $0.011/kWh electricity tax on data centers effective July 2026. Citi maintains Buy on both EQIX and DLR, concluding the tax is immaterial as costs pass through to hyperscale/wholesale customers. DLR announced ~$1.6B in three transactions: 1,440 acres near Kansas City with 2GW capacity, increased Teraco ownership to 77% for $650M, and acquired Columbia Capital ($485M). MS maintains Equal-weight on DLR at $215 PT, preferring OW EQIX.

bullets.title: TGT: Wolfe upgrades to Outperform/Top Pick at $162; store resets gaining traction
bullets.body: Wolfe Research upgraded TGT to Outperform and named it Top Pick with $162 PT (+15%), citing accelerating store resets, improving new customer growth (+4.1% over past 4 weeks vs -8.0% prior 52 weeks), and EPS estimates too low ($8.48 vs $8.37 consensus). Traffic data shows TGT 2QTD foot traffic +4.5%. Stock scores 10/10 on Wolfe's MALTA quantitative model and trades at 16.6x forward earnings vs WMT at 37.4x. Simultaneously, Wolfe downgraded FIVE and HD to Peer Perform.

bullets.title: FOXA: World Cup driving ~$500M in Q4/Q1 advertising; UBS raises estimates, maintains Buy
bullets.body: UBS raised FOXA F4Q total company ad revenue growth estimate to +31% YoY (from +28%), incorporating ~$500M in soccer advertising across F4Q/F1Q vs prior $350M. Full-year EBITDA expected at record $3.7B despite non-election year. FOX One downloads up >15x June vs May. Shares trade below 5x 2027/2028 standalone EBITDA. F27 cyclical tailwinds include World Cup knockout stage and midterm elections.

bullets.title: CMCSA: Sky nearing $2.2B ITV M&E acquisition; broadband outlook remains pressured
bullets.body: Comcast's Sky unit is nearing agreement to acquire ITV's Media & Entertainment business for ~£1.6B ($2.2B) to strengthen UK streaming. UBS 2Q preview models 153K broadband losses and ARPU declines accelerating to -4.0%. Peacock expected to reach profitability in 2Q. CHTR accelerating losses to 166K in 2Q; 2026 full-year broadband loss forecast 526K.

bullets.title: T/VZ: VZ wins AWS-3 reauction paying $3.2B for 82 licenses; AT&T raises $0.011/kWh fee
bullets.body: Verizon was the largest winner in the FCC AWS-3 reauction (Auction 113), purchasing 82 licenses in major markets for $3.2B of the $3.56B total. T-Mobile won 102 licenses for $277.8M. Separately, AT&T raised its Administrative & Regulatory Cost Recovery Fee by $1/month per line effective August 5—KeyBanc estimates ~$900M in annualized revenue uplift with minimal churn risk, maintaining Overweight at $36 PT.

bullets.title: GEV/CEG/VST: Power bottleneck theme; CVX/MSFT 20-year BTM deal; DOE commits $17.5B nuclear loans
bullets.body: Chevron and Microsoft signed a 20-year 2.67GW gas power deal (Project Kilby) near Pecos, TX for data center supply, with first power by 2028. DOE announced $17.5B conditional loan commitments for 10 Westinghouse AP1000 reactors. Walmart signed 176MW nuclear PPA with Constellation for Dresden facility starting 2029. Jefferies downgraded TLN to Hold at $453 PT after robust run. EPC contractor PRIM slashed guidance 39% on six solar project cost overruns.

bullets.title: AMD/ARM: UBS raises AMD PT to $670, ARM to $470 on agentic AI CPU demand
bullets.body: UBS raised AMD PT to $670 (from $455) and ARM to $470 (from $260), citing agentic AI driving architectural split with ARM favored for latency-sensitive head nodes and AMD favored for throughput-driven standalone racks. UBS raised AMD CY30 server CPU revenue to $50B from $41B. QCOM Investor Day raised FY29 non-handset revenue target to $40B (from $22B) including $15B data center; META confirmed as QCOM CPU customer; DZ Bank upgraded QCOM to Buy at $265 PT.

bullets.title: AFRM: Mizuho survey shows Walmart customers prefer Affirm 2x over Klarna; MS downgrades
bullets.body: Mizuho survey of ~450 Walmart shoppers found 41% prefer Affirm vs 36% Klarna overall, with online-first shoppers preferring Affirm 2x (24% vs 12%). Mizuho raised AFRM PT to $100 (Outperform). Separately, Morgan Stanley downgraded AFRM to Equal-Weight, arguing the market now properly reflects growth durability; analyst is 30% above Street on FY28 EPS at $3.37.

bullets.title: FIG: Config 2026 launches AI canvas; Wolfe reiterates Peer Perform; Citi upgrades to Buy
bullets.body: Figma's Config 2026 conference showcased Code Layers, Motion, Shaders, and an intelligent agentic layer. Citi upgraded FIG to Buy with $36 PT (93% upside), citing broader platform potential. Wolfe maintained Peer Perform, noting AI monetization pace is tempered by competition (Claude Code, Cursor) and mixed Make reviews. Time-in-canvas leaking to AI-native coding tools; JPM maintains Neutral flagging near-term gross margin pressure from free beta features.
